Total portfolio area is approximately 53,530 square feet, with a weighted average remaining lease term of approximately 11.3 years and year-one scheduled base rent equal to $23.01 per square foot.

The portfolio comprises three CVS pharmacies — Charleston, West Virginia (11,816 sf, 14.5 years of term remaining), Millbrook, Alabama (10,522 sf, 9.1 years) and Hoover, Alabama (10,364 sf, 9.1 years) — and three Pinnacle Bank branches in North Carolina: Eastchester Drive, High Point (9,230 sf, 11.4 years), Westchester Drive, High Point (3,692 sf, 11.4 years) and Thomasville (7,906 sf, 11.2 years). All six leases carry fixed-rate renewal options extending as far as 2061.

The Trust acquired the properties from unaffiliated third-party sellers on February 17, 2026, financed with an $8,855,000 loan from Provident Bank. Interests are offered at $1,000 each with a 50-Interest ($50,000) minimum, the lowest minimum in our current inventory. Sponsor: ARCTRUST Private Capital, an affiliate of the ARCTRUST Group of Companies, a vertically integrated real estate organisation responsible for developing, acquiring or joint-venture funding over 500 projects worth more than $5 billion across 40 years. Projections reflect the Trust Manager's forecast; there is no guarantee that this offering will meet its investment objectives.
notes:
Two things distinguish this offering. It was genuinely well bought — the price paid for the six properties sits below the BDO appraised value, which is unusual — and it is the only offering in our current inventory whose projected distribution declines across the hold. The decline is not an operating problem; income rises every year. It is the end of the interest-only period and the start of amortisation. That is not a loss of value, since the loan balance falls and total economic return keeps rising, but a client who buys on the year-one figure will see cash yield step down in Year 6 and stay down.

The unhedged reset is the item to press on. The rate resets automatically at the five-year and seven-year marks to the 2-year Treasury plus 200 basis points, subject to a 5.75% floor, and the projection carries the floor rate throughout. Ask for the same forecast at 6.5% and at 7.5%.

Tenant credit is narrower than the property count suggests: six properties, two tenant credits, three each. The Trust owns all six in a single entity and the Memorandum states it will need to sell all of them at the same time, so there is no partial-exit flexibility. Capital reserves are minimal and the Lender requires none, while the Trust remains liable if a tenant fails to pay a property operating expense.

Treat the marketing fact sheet with care: it states a hold period the Memorandum contradicts, and it labels a leverage ratio "Loan-to-Purchase Price" when the figure is loan to total capitalisation. Use the Memorandum. The Memorandum also contains four internal arithmetic and dating defects, none of which changes a distribution figure but all of which are listed in the source notes.

The sponsor's disclosed record is four exits with internal rates of return ranging from 1.99% to 28.65%, with no hold periods or equity multiples given, so there is no reliable central tendency to quote. The Trust Manager and Depositor on this offering are newly formed and have no prior performance of their own.

exit721Route:
The FMV Option is the exit mechanism, and it is cash-by-default with a Units election - the mirror image of the NexPoint structures. Beginning two years after the Offering Termination Date, the Trust Manager "has the right, but not the obligation, to acquire the Interests... for either (i) cash or (ii) units in an entity organized or identified by the Trust Manager or an Affiliate (an 'Exchange Entity')." Holders receive cash unless a Holder affirmatively elects Units AND meets the Exchange Entity's investor suitability requirements. So the default outcome is a taxable event for a 1031 purchaser, and the tax-deferred route requires both an election and qualification.

The Exchange Entity is undefined. There is no named REIT, no named operating partnership, no disclosed structure and no indication of what the Units would represent, what they would yield, or whether any market would exist for them - only "an entity organized or identified by the Trust Manager or an Affiliate." That is the same vagueness flagged on NexPoint Marina I, Marina II and Small Bay III, and the same question applies: a client cannot evaluate an exchange into an entity that does not yet exist. Ask what the Exchange Entity is expected to be before treating this as a 721 landing place.

The valuation mechanic contains a haircut worth understanding. Consideration equals the Holder's percentage interest multiplied by the value of the Projects, where that value is the gross fair market value REDUCED BY "any and all secured or unsecured liabilities and accounts payable" and by amounts payable to the Trust Manager or its Affiliates at the time the Interests are transferred, then INCREASED BY reserves, cash and accounts receivable. Compare NexPoint Waterford, where fair market value is struck with "no discounts for lack of liquidity or minority interests" applied. Gross fair market value is set by one or more MAI appraisers with at least five years' experience in the relevant market areas, who have 30 days to determine value, with closing within 30 days of that determination.

Practical read: treat this as a cash-exit offering with an optional and currently unspecifiable 721 alternative, not as a planned UPREIT roll-up. The base case remains a sale of the six Projects within nine years, driven by the loan maturity. Not tax advice.

IDEAL Ecco Park DST is a $45,670,000 offering owning Ecco Park Apartments, a 360-unit garden-style multifamily community at 3461 Huddle Way, Canal Winchester, Ohio, in the Columbus metropolitan area. CONSTRUCTED IN 2024, the community comprises fifteen three-storey buildings totalling approximately 373,548 net rentable square feet on roughly 23.73 acres, plus a clubhouse and six garage buildings, with one-, two- and three-bedroom floorplans. Unit features include gourmet island kitchens, stainless appliances, luxury vinyl flooring, double vanities and in-unit washer/dryers in select units; community amenities include a resort-style pool, 24-hour fitness centre, clubhouse with coffee bar, dog park, walking and biking trails, playground, controlled key-fob access and attached garages.

The Trust is the beneficial owner of a fee simple interest and acquired the property from an unaffiliated third party on March 24, 2026, financed with a $48,855,000 loan from Walker & Dunlop under the Freddie Mac Capital Markets Execution Program, assigned at closing to Freddie Mac. The loan carries a 5.17% fixed rate over a ten-year term maturing April 1, 2036, interest-only for the first five years and then fully amortising, with the first principal payment due May 1, 2031. The property benefits from a long-term Community Reinvestment Area property tax abatement (see the highlights below). Property management is performed by Coastal Ridge Management, LLC, an unaffiliated third-party operator headquartered in Columbus. Sponsor: IDEAL Capital Group Holdings, LLC, a California multifamily investment firm that with its affiliates has developed and acquired over $3 billion of real estate representing more than 15,000 units across a 36-year history. Projections reflect the Sponsor's Financial Forecast; there is no guarantee that this offering will meet its investment objectives.
notes:
The price on this offering is substantially a capitalised tax abatement, and the abatement's compliance conditions are the thing to examine.

CBRE appraised the property at $83,800,000, but that figure includes $13,310,000 of net present value attributable to the tax abatement and $1,620,000 of furniture, fixtures and equipment. On the real property alone the appraisal is approximately $68,870,000. The abatement's net present value by itself is 29.1% of the entire equity raise, so the client is buying a property-tax subsidy as much as a building.

The Community Reinvestment Area Agreement with the City of Columbus requires 72 of the 360 units — 20% — to be restricted, 36 at or below 80% of area median income and 36 at or below 100%. The Memorandum's own footnote describes only the 100% tier as restricted, and says the 80% tier is satisfied because market rent currently sits below the cap. Rent growth and the abatement's rent caps therefore pull against each other on a fifth of the units, with 29% of equity value behind the outcome. The penalty for a shortfall runs from 20% to 90% of the annual tax abated. Request the current abatement compliance file: which units are designated at each tier, the current Franklin County caps, actual in-place rents on those units, and the headroom before a restriction binds.

Compounding it, the Master Tenant bears uncontrollable expenses — taxes, utilities, insurance — only up to the projected level set out in the Financial Forecast. Above that the Memorandum states the Trust is responsible for the difference through a reduction in Additional Rent or Bonus Rent. A property-tax surprise therefore reaches distributions directly, on a deal whose pricing case rests on a property-tax subsidy.

On the forecast itself: the distribution dips in year six, from 5.21% to 4.74%, and the cause is the loan rather than the property. Net operating income rises in every year of the ten-year forecast. The loan is interest-only for five years and begins amortising in year six, which lifts annual debt service by roughly $673,000 in one step. A client should expect that dip and understand it is scheduled, not a downside case.

The genuine positives: the asset was built in 2024, so there is no property improvement plan, no deferred maintenance and no renovation year; the property manager is a substantial genuinely unaffiliated third party; and Columbus fundamentals are strong. Two document items need resolution — title insurance is written materially below total capitalisation, and the abatement's fifteen-year clock is dated two inconsistent ways within the Memorandum. The property condition report identified elevated short-term radon readings in a number of units and recommended long-term testing. There is no 721 exit, and a Springing LLC conversion would end 1031 eligibility with no fallback language in the document.

exit721Route:
No 721 or UPREIT exit is offered. The only appearance of Code Section 721 in this Memorandum is the tax treatment of a Transfer Distribution into a "Springing LLC" - the protective conversion the Administrative Trustee may be required to make to avoid a loan default or loss of the Property. The Memorandum notes such a transfer "generally should not be subject to federal income tax pursuant to Code Section 721" but could attract state or local income, transfer or other taxes, and that there is no assurance it remains non-taxable federally when it occurs.

Critically, that conversion ends 1031 eligibility outright: "If the Trust is converted into a Springing LLC or the Property is contributed to a Springing LLC, the Investors' ownership Interests in the Springing LLC will not qualify for tax-deferred exchange treatment under Section 1031." Unlike the LSC-Fort Washington Memorandum, this one offers no fallback language about the manager converting Springing LLC interests back into direct property interests - it simply states the interests will not qualify. So the downside scenario that triggers conversion also terminates the exchange chain, with no disclosed remedy.

The Trust's stated objectives are to distribute annual cash flow, manage the Property to maintain long-term value, and "sell the Property prior to the Maturity Date of the Loan (i.e., April 1, 2036)." The brochure confirms the mechanics: "Upon the disposition of the Property, the Trust shall distribute all of its assets to the beneficial interest holders of the Trust, and then dissolve the Trust." A single sale, a distribution, and a dissolution - the investor then places the proceeds into a new exchange or takes the gain.

Practical read for an exchange client: plan on a sale by 2036 and a subsequent exchange; clients who need a 721 landing place should be shown a NexPoint, Bluerock or Cantor structure. Not tax advice.

JWCM Vivian, DST is a $46,170,900 offering owning "The Vivian," a 325-unit mid-rise multifamily community at 1246 Allene Avenue Southwest, Atlanta, Georgia, with direct access to the Atlanta BeltLine. The property comprises three buildings of three, four and five storeys on approximately 8.471 acres, with roughly 264,136 square feet of net leasable residential area and 378 parking spaces including six EV spaces. Amenities include a swimming pool, fitness centre, grilling area, coffee shop, dog park, EV charging, meeting space and lounge, yoga room and clubhouse.

The Trust acquired the property from an unaffiliated third party on August 21, 2025, financed with a $47,189,000 Fannie Mae DUS loan from KeyBank National Association at a 5.30% fixed rate, interest-only until September 1, 2032 and then amortising through its September 1, 2035 maturity. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL NOTE: the property participates in the Fulton County Development Authority's bond-lease tax abatement programme, under which the Development Authority holds fee title and leases the land and improvements to the Trust; the Trust is obligated to acquire fee simple ownership when the Bond Lease expires. The Trust therefore holds a LEASEHOLD interest rather than fee title during the hold, and the Memorandum directs each prospective purchaser to seek advice from a qualified tax advisor on the implications for a Section 1031 exchange. Tax counsel has opined that purchasers, not the Development Authority, should be treated as the true owners of the property for federal income tax purposes. Property management is performed by RangeWater Residential, LLC, a third-party operator. Sponsor: JWCM Exchange I, LLC, an affiliate of Jesselson Warsavsky Capital Management, LLC. Projections reflect the Sponsor's Financial Forecast; there is no guarantee that this offering will meet its investment objectives.
notes:
The two facts that shape this offering are the abatement and the estate.

The Fulton County bond-lease abatement does not run flat. It starts at 50% of the tax saving and steps down five points a year, so property tax expense rises in every year of the hold. That is visible in the Master Lease table without needing the forecast: Base Rent climbs more than 75% across the ten years, and essentially all of the early increase is tax escrow rather than income to the Trust. The Supplemental Rent Breakpoint rises 39% over the same period, which means gross revenue must grow 39% simply to keep the investor tier the same size. That is why the projected floor sits below the Year-1 figure. The Additional Rent cap is flat at $1,884,300 for all ten years, equal to 4.08% of equity, printed as a constant rather than as a growing figure.

The Trust holds a LEASEHOLD, not fee title. The Development Authority holds fee title during the abatement period and the Trust is obligated to acquire fee simple ownership when the Bond Lease expires. The mitigants here are stronger than on comparable leasehold offerings: tax counsel opines that purchasers "should" be treated as the true owners for federal income tax purposes, the structure is more than a decade established and has been vetted by lenders and institutions, and the Memorandum states there is no net economic cost during the lease because the Trust's rent to the Authority and the Authority's bond payments offset exactly. "Should" is not "will", and a client's own tax adviser should confirm it in writing before an exchange is placed.

Two Memorandum passages should be read by the client's adviser directly rather than summarised. The Memorandum discloses that the Trust "will be subject to immediate dilution and the Beneficial Owners may recover less than their invested capital upon any eventual sale of the Property." It also warns that the IRS could treat part of the purchase price, and possibly the reserves, as boot in a Section 1031 exchange. The price paid for the real estate was within a fraction of a percent of the Newmark appraised value — the tightest such spread in our current inventory.

The workforce-housing restriction here is a marketing obligation rather than a rent cap: roughly 15% of units must be actively marketed to Workforce Residents, and a unit counts toward the requirement even if marketing does not place one. The property manager is third-party. The Memorandum is dated September 2025, the oldest in our current inventory — confirm the offering is still open and ask whether any supplement has been issued.

No 721 or UPREIT exit is disclosed in the document available, and the exit analysis here is incomplete - the field is marked Unclear rather than None for that reason. The reduced Memorandum obtained from Google Drive omits the Trust Agreement (Exhibit B) and the full Summary of the Trust Agreement, which is where an exchange right, fair-market-value option or sponsor purchase option would be defined if one exists. Nothing in the available text describes any such mechanism. The Sponsor's stated objectives are simply to preserve capital, make monthly distributions, and "sell the Property at a profit within approximately five to ten years," and the only Code Section 721 context that appears concerns a Transfer Distribution to a Springing LLC - the defensive conversion the Manager may be required to effect, which the Memorandum links to the risk that "prior to the maturity date of the Loan, the Trust may be required to effectuate a Transfer Distribution." What IS clear, and unusual, is the exit obligation created by the bond-lease structure. On expiration of the Bond Lease the Trust is contractually obligated to acquire fee simple ownership of the Property from the Fulton County Development Authority. For a DST - which cannot raise new capital, renegotiate debt or refinance - an obligation to purchase a fee interest is a structural commitment that must be satisfied out of existing assets or resolved by selling before it falls due. Establish the Bond Lease expiration date relative to the 1 September 2035 loan maturity and the five-to-ten-year sale objective, and confirm the mechanics and cost of the unwind. The Memorandum describes the unwind as automatic - "the structure is automatically unwound to establish fee ownership in the Trust" - and states there is no net economic cost during the lease because the Trust's rent to the Authority and the Authority's bond payments to the Trust offset exactly. Confirm that the same is true of the unwind itself, including any Georgia transfer tax or recording cost on the conveyance of fee title.

Put that opinion in front of the client's own tax adviser in writing before placing an exchange, and note that the interest a buyer would acquire on a mid-hold sale is likewise a leasehold. exit721Route:
Named counterparty, which is the main improvement over the other NexPoint Offerings in this workbook. NexPoint Diversified Real Estate Trust ("NXDT") acts through its Operating Partnership, a Delaware limited partnership, which holds the right - but not the obligation - to require each Beneficial Owner to exchange Interests for OP Units in a transaction intended to qualify under Code Section 721 or 351. Compare Marina I, Marina II and Small Bay III, where the "Exchange Entity" is defined only as "the Manager, its affiliates, successors, or assigns" with no named vehicle.

Who elects: the Operating Partnership, not the investor. It may exercise the Exchange Right only after Beneficial Owners have held their Interests for one year. Exercise is by a Notice of Exchange in the form attached to the Trust Agreement, followed by a 90-day standstill during which none of the Manager, the Trust, the Beneficial Owners or the Operating Partnership may solicit, negotiate or consummate any competing transaction involving the Trust or the Trust Estate.

Cash route: available, but by affirmative election on a short clock. A Beneficial Owner who does not want OP Units ("Dissenting Beneficial Owner") may elect to have the Operating Partnership acquire its Interests for cash at then fair market value, but must give written notice within 30 days of the date the Manager mails the Notice of Exchange. Silence is consent: an owner who does not deliver a Dissenting Notice within 30 days "will be deemed to have agreed to the exercise of the Exchange Right by the Operating Partnership for cash." Note the direction of that default - failing to respond does not leave you in the Trust and does not get you OP Units; it puts you in cash, which is a taxable event for a 1031 purchaser. An owner who fails to execute the required documents is likewise not admitted as a limited partner and is cashed out. Diarise the 30 days. No cap on the cash election is disclosed.

Valuation: fair market value equals the owner's percentage of Interests multiplied by the value of the Property as determined by an independent appraisal firm the Manager selects in its sole discretion, completed within one year of the exercise date. No discount for lack of liquidity or for minority interest is applied - a meaningful investor protection. Unlike Marina II, the appraisal basis is sound here: the Trust owns the fee interest in the Property, so the appraised asset is the asset being valued.

Tax protection: discretionary only. The Operating Partnership "may, but is under no obligation to" provide a Tax Protection Agreement under which it would agree not to dispose of the Property within two years in a transaction triggering Section 704(c) gain, and to indemnify for taxes if it does. Ask whether one will be offered before relying on it.

After the exchange: OP Units are exchangeable for cash or NXDT shares, at the Operating Partnership's election as to form, after a one-year holding period. NXDT declared a distribution on 29 July 2025 and the Sponsor expects OP Unit holders to receive distributions substantially equivalent to NXDT shareholders. Once the Exchange Right is exercised, a subsequent individual Section 1031 exchange is no longer available - the investor is in a partnership interest, not real property. Liquidity in OP Units and NXDT shares is limited and subject to market volatility. Not tax advice.

exit721Route:
No 721 or UPREIT exit is offered. The only reference to Code Section 721 in this Memorandum concerns the federal tax treatment of a Transfer Distribution - the conversion of the Trust into a Springing LLC, which the Administrative Trustee may effect in a distress scenario. The Memorandum notes such a transfer generally should not be subject to federal income tax under Section 721 but "could be subject, however, to state or local" taxes. That is a protective mechanism, not a liquidity option an investor can elect, and it is not an UPREIT roll-up: there is no operating partnership, no named REIT counterparty, no exchange right, no OP Units and no sponsor cash-purchase election anywhere in the structure.

The Trust's stated objectives are explicit and limited: acquire and lease the Property to the Master Tenant, pay regular distributions out of net cash flows, preserve the intrinsic value of the Property, and sell the Property. A single exit, by sale, with proceeds distributed for the investor to place into a new exchange. No anticipated hold period is disclosed. The Franchise Agreement expires 30 July 2046, and note that a sale during the Franchise Term requires the buyer to be an approved IHG franchisee or to negotiate a new franchise, which narrows the buyer pool relative to an unencumbered asset.

The Offering does, however, carry a sale-proceeds hurdle at exit: the Master Tenant's economics on a sale are subordinated until the net sales price equals or exceeds the full offering amount, so investors are made whole on their entire subscription first. That aligns the Sponsor's exit incentive with investors recovering their full subscription, which is a meaningful substitute for the optionality a 721 structure provides - though it does not solve the reinvestment problem for a client who wants to leave the 1031 treadmill. Practical read for an exchange client: plan on a sale and a subsequent exchange. Investors who need a 721 landing place should be shown a NexPoint, Bluerock or Cantor structure instead. exit721Route:
There is no 721 exchange, no UPREIT, and no exchange right of any kind. The exit is a straight sale of the Property at the Signatory Trustee's sole discretion. The Trust terminates on the earlier of that sale or a Transfer Distribution. Holders have no vote: the PPM states the sale "will occur without regard" to Holder approval, and while the Signatory Trustee may poll Holders, they "have no formal voting rights with respect to" it.

The only reference to Code Section 721 in the document is the springing-LLC mechanic, and it must not be mistaken for an UPREIT option. If a Transfer Distribution occurs, the Property moves to a Springing LLC taxed as a partnership, membership interests are distributed to the Beneficial Owners, and the Trust terminates. That transfer should itself be tax-free under Section 721, but the consequence for the investor is the opposite of an UPREIT: the PPM warns that "the Holders may lose their ability to participate in a future Code Section 1031 exchange." It is a defensive conversion used when the Trust would otherwise be forced to act beyond a DST's permitted powers, not a liquidity route.

So model this as a single-asset, single-exit, all-cash hold with no built-in continuation into a REIT and no disclosed redemption or repurchase programme.

notes:
This is not a Delaware statutory trust. It is an offering of undivided mineral interests and non-participating royalty interests in oil and gas properties, sold as direct-title units, and it is carried in our comparison because it is marketed as Section 1031 replacement property and competes for the same exchange dollars.

The structural 1031 position is better than the label suggests, and the supporting evidence is worse. What is being sold is the right thing: mineral interests and non-participating royalty interests are perpetual interests in the mineral estate, hence real property under Texas and Oklahoma law, and investors take deeded direct title as co-owners, which keeps the offering outside the partnership-interest exclusion. The Memorandum deliberately excludes overriding royalty interests and explains why — an overriding royalty terminates when the underlying lease terminates. But the cover page states only that the Offeror "has secured a tax opinion" that an undivided interest "should" be treated as real property, and that opinion is not attached, not summarised, and its author, date and assumptions are not disclosed. The Memorandum's substantive tax section contains no Section 1031 discussion at all. OBTAIN THE OPINION IN WRITING AND HAVE THE CLIENT'S OWN TAX COUNSEL REVIEW IT BEFORE ANY EXCHANGE IS PLACED. This is not tax advice.

Exhibit A is missing. The Memorandum directs the reader to it nine times — for the properties, the wells, the legal descriptions and the type-curve analysis — and the section headed "Overview of the Properties in this Offering" consists of a single line pointing to it. A search of all 108 pages returns no legal descriptions, no well names and no API numbers. An investor taking deeded title cannot identify from this document which interests they are buying, which for a 45-day replacement-property identification is not an academic problem. Request Exhibit A before anything else.

The prior performance section contains no data. It is roughly 1,000 characters, all of it disclaimer, for a sponsor that states elsewhere in the same document that it has formed and managed 27 investment funds and raised approximately $204,000,000 across more than 490 properties. Sixteen years of operating history, none of it disclosed. Ask for realised distribution and disposition results on Funds 1 through 27 before recommending Fund 28.

On the price deck: the base range is effectively the 2028 forward strip flat-lined, with gas haircut below it, which is a defensible and mildly conservative construction for the five forecast years. The assumption to challenge is the terminal one — the "to life" row, which values everything beyond 2030 and therefore most of a 35-year asset, holds oil and natural gas liquids at the 2026 strip in perpetuity, roughly 15% above the 2030 strip. Ask for the reserve report and for a sensitivity holding the 2030 strip flat to life.

The genuine structural advantage is control. There is no 721 mechanism, no operating partnership, no exchange entity, no fair market value option and no springing LLC, and none is needed: the deed is in the investor's hands, the manager cannot sell an interest without that holder's written consent, and each owner can exchange again on their own timetable. The cost of that freedom is liquidity — the Memorandum concedes there is no formal market for fractional mineral and royalty interests. Income is entirely commodity-price dependent with no floor and no disclosed hedge, existing wells decline naturally, the holding is non-operating, there is no fixed hold period and no defined exit, and there is no tenant, lease or contractual rent of any kind. Two return targets sit two paragraphs apart in the document and do not agree.

There is no operating partnership, no REIT, no Exchange Entity, no FMV Option and no Code Section 721 anywhere in this offering. The word does not appear in the Memorandum.
